key_insight: CiteGuard-RAG shows that retrieval alone is not enough for trustworthy RAG: answers must also be validated for grounding, citation correctness, and refusal behavior. Its runtime validation pipeline helps produce more reliable, evidence-based responses.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the gap between getting relevant documents and actually generating answers that are grounded in those documents, correctly cited, and safely refused when evidence is insufficient.
method: Uses hybrid semantic + lexical retrieval to improve evidence collection.
Constrains generation so answers must follow available citations.
Validates each sentence for grounding at runtime and triggers single-pass regeneration when needed.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work highlights a practical path toward more trustworthy RAG systems with fewer unsupported claims and better citation fidelity. It is especially relevant for applications where evidence quality, traceability, and refusal behavior matter.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing retrieval -> constrained generation -> sentence-level validation -> regeneration
Side-by-side comparison of grounded vs. ungrounded answers with citations highlighted
Validation checklist icon set for grounding, citation validity, and refusal detection
Flowchart illustrating when the system accepts an answer or regenerates it
paper_title: CiteGuard-RAG: A Validation-Centered AI System for Evidence-Grounded Question Answering
paper_authors: Sumit Barua, Guan Hong, Halil Dursunoglu, Charles Rodgers, Alvis Fong
